page.summary: Cover chase, generators and rescue without betting on strangers to fill the gaps. Change jobs when the team needs something else.

verdict.recommendation: A dependable Solo Q starting point when you do not know your teammates' plans.
verdict.soloQ: Choose independent coverage, then use the information you actually have to avoid duplicated rescues and idle time.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Still usable, but agree who covers each job; spreading the same tools across everyone gives up the benefit of planned roles.
verdict.mainWeakness: Covering several problems leaves less room to specialize in any one of them.

notes.whyItsHere: Turn a usable vault into a route away from the current tile, so one chase does not consume every nearby resource.
Give yourself an objective target when nobody is calling generators, instead of leaving the dangerous cluster until last.
Keep a personal answer to being picked up again after an unhook; it is insurance for that situation, not permission to take unnecessary hits.
Choose one: solve uncertainty about who is rescuing, or improve the recovery after your own rescue.

optionReasons.whyItsHere: Choose this when knowing whether another teammate is approaching the hook is more valuable than committing blindly yourself.
Choose this when you expect to take unhooks and help the rescued teammate return to useful play, rather than leaving them injured.

opening: Check the highlighted generator cluster and a usable escape route before settling into repair. Reassess your job at each hook or chase change.

rows.situation: Nobody needs an immediate rescue and you are free to repair.
rows.action: Work on an accessible highlighted generator that helps break up the cluster. If the Killer makes it unsafe, rotate rather than feeding a hit for the highlight.
rows.why: Objective information should remove indecision, not force commitment to a defended location.

rows.situation: The Killer is closing in and you have a usable vault with Lithe available.
rows.action: Choose your next route before vaulting, then spend the escape on distance to that route instead of circling back into the same pressure.
rows.why: A mobility tool buys useful time only when you have somewhere to go.

rows.situation: A teammate is hooked and you chose Kindred.
rows.action: Check who is already moving toward the hook. Keep repairing if the rescue is covered; approach if it is not, adjusting for any Killer information you can see.
rows.why: Sending everyone to one rescue abandons the other jobs this loadout is meant to cover.

rows.situation: You made the unhook and chose We'll Make It.
rows.action: Offer the rescued teammate a heal where the Killer cannot immediately interrupt. If the Killer returns, move apart and escape instead of insisting on finishing under pressure.
rows.why: The recovery is valuable when it gets a teammate back into the Trial, not when it creates two vulnerable targets.

rows.situation: You have just been unhooked and the Killer is still pursuing you.
rows.action: Prioritize an escape route and be ready for the pickup Skill Check if Will to Live is still active. Once the pursuit ends, return to a useful job deliberately rather than treating the protection as permanent.
rows.why: Its limited post-unhook opportunity cannot support an entire match plan; check its availability before relying on it.

abortWhen: If a teammate has already covered the rescue or reset you were approaching, stop duplicating it and take the unattended generator or other open job.
When your safety perk is unavailable, especially after the gates are powered, choose routes and rescues on their own merits rather than banking on a second escape.

weaknesses: You still need teammates to convert your chase time into progress; flexibility cannot supply all four players' work.
commonMistakes: Rushed-vaulting casually before a chase and then planning an escape around unavailable Lithe.
Treating the fourth slot as both information and healing at once; play around the option you equipped.
Repairing or taking another Conspicuous Action, then assuming Will to Live remains active against a returning Killer.

soloQ: Use visible teammate activity and hook information to choose an uncovered job; the Intent System helps but does not guarantee that someone will complete it.
coordinatedSwf: Call the job you are taking before rotating, so flexibility fills a gap instead of pulling a second player off the same generator.
